mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 7% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% coincident with a rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a cooling housing market amid inflationary pressure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is held constant at or below 0.25% for six consecutive months, monetary policy is effectively constrained, which tends to support risk asset valuations and produce positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) to below 5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth accelerates above 200,000 monthly indicates a tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) grow less than 1% signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in economic activity and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 5% AND GDPC1 YoY change < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
